feedback: No race data or earlier candidate exists yet, so nothing below is evidence from a race. Your baseline is symmetric and well sampled. The controller I wrote assumes the five sensors read the line cleanly. The main unknowns are the forward offset and the track width. If the next race shows low rms_error and few line_loss_events but a completion_time above 3 s or no completion, the limit is speed, not sensing. In that case keep the sensor layout and try a higher wheel_radius or a lighter mass so the robot reaches speed with less drive. If the next race shows high steering_oscillation or max_error, especially on the slalom, the sensing is reacting too late or too sharply. In that case try moving the sensors closer to the axle (y 0.02 to 0.03 m) or reducing the sensor pitch so the readings change more smoothly. If line_loss_events are high on the tighter bends, widen the track (0.14 to 0.16 m) for more turn authority at the same mass.
requested_changes: If completion_time is above 3 s or the run does not complete while rms_error stays low: try wheel_radius 0.035 and mass 0.7 kg to raise achievable speed and reduce the drive needed (no earlier race evidence yet; this is the intended first test).

If steering_oscillation or max_error is high on the slalom: try sensor y positions at 0.02 m instead of 0.04 m so the sensors react closer to the axle and the controller is not reacting to the line too late (no earlier race evidence yet).
If line_loss_events are high on the tighter bends: try wheel_track 0.14 m to increase turn authority, keeping the same sensor layout (no earlier race evidence yet).
